headline: Heads of Security reports learned attention gates that improve prompt-injection robustness in two open-weight models
summary: The preprint introduces Heads of Security (HoS), which learns small per-head attention gates to separate trusted instructions from untrusted content while allowing the model to reason over that content. On Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct and GPT-OSS-20B, the authors report lower adaptive RL-Hammer attack success against HoS than against an undefended base model or SecAlign++, with means over five runs on 100 held-out InjecAgent goals where available. The official project page shows a mixed utility picture: Llama AgentDyn utility is 18.3% for HoS versus 33.7% for the base model, despite lower reported attack success, while Llama AgentDojo utility is 58.5% versus 53.7%. These remain author-reported results in two open-weight model settings, not independent replication or a deployment-safety result. A checksum-matched PyPI 0.1.0 source distribution uploaded October 8 contains package code, tests and demos for both model families; this activation inspected it but did not execute it, and PyPI reports no build provenance.
